name: fetch-policy
description: Origin policy for model-triggered HTTP: allow/ask/deny per scheme://host[:port], with persisted approvals

enabled.description: Whether the origin policy is active. Set false to remove the layer entirely.

default.description: What an origin no rule matches does. "ask" prompts: allow once / allow origin for session / always allow (persisted to <config-dir>/fetch-policy.json) / deny; fail-closed deny with the exact allow-line when no interactive UI can answer (one-shot, CI). "allow" is the permissive posture plus explicit denies; "deny" is allowlist-only.

allow.description: Origins to allow without asking. Grammar: 'scheme://host[:port]' -- '*' globs (a leading '*.example.com' also matches the bare apex, never evil-example.com); an omitted port means the scheme's default port, ':*' any port. No paths: HTTPS paths are invisible without MITM, so path rules would be a lie. Merged with persisted approvals from <config-dir>/fetch-policy.json.

deny.description: Origins to block without asking. Deny beats allow and cannot be overridden from a prompt or the state file -- denies live here only.

proxyEnabled.description: Expose the policy proxy for child-process injection (tool exec plane, stdio MCP servers). Loopback-only and token-authenticated; binds only once a spawn actually asks for it. False = never expose it.

proxyAskTimeoutMs.description: How long a child-process connection waits at an approval prompt before being denied. A prompt nobody answers must not hang the child forever.

hardEgress.description: Kernel-enforce the policy for children instead of merely injecting it: exec-plane entries and stdio MCP servers boot in a private network namespace whose ONLY exit is the policy proxy (a fixed jail-loopback port piped over a unix socket). Tools that ignore proxy env then get no network at all, and deny means denied for raw sockets too. Requires Linux with working bwrap AND unprivileged user namespaces; when either is missing every child spawn is REFUSED (it never degrades to the cooperative proxy). Costs: host loopback (dev servers on 127.0.0.1) is unreachable from children, and inline-mode (toolExec: inline) spawns are refused while it is on.

hardEgressLoopback.description: Under hardEgress, whether connects to loopback origins are denied outright (false, the default) or enter the normal allow/ask/deny flow like any other origin (true). With true, a child's connect to http://127.0.0.1:3000 asks -- and reachability is restored for approved loopback services.
